title: Hence the common Roman conclusion: God concurs proximately and immediately with every act; but how is disputed
source_text: IX. Ex his & similibus, communi jam fere consensu, concludunt Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae Deum cum causis omnibus secundis, sive necessariis, sive liberis, aut contingentibus, ad singulos earum actus concurrere & cooperari, & quidem proxime & immediate. Attamen quum quaeritur quae sit illa causae primae cum causa secunda cooperatio, & qua in re consistat, magna reperitur inter Doctores Scholasticos sententiarum varietas.
pass_a_gloss: From these and similar things, by a now almost common consent, the Doctors of the Roman Church conclude that God concurs and cooperates with all second causes, whether necessary, or free, or contingent, to each of their acts, and that proximately and immediately. And yet when it is asked what that cooperation of the first cause with the second cause is, and in what thing it consists, a great variety of opinions is found among the Scholastic Doctors.
pass_b_english: From these and like arguments the teachers of the Roman Church now conclude, almost unanimously, that God concurs and cooperates with every secondary cause, necessary, free or contingent, in each of its acts, and does so proximately and immediately.
But when one asks what this cooperation of the first cause with the secondary cause is and what it consists in, the scholastic teachers turn out to hold widely different views.

lemmas.gloss: by a now almost common consent

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
